data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Wart & antiviral agents_

**Class:** Caustic organic acid (protein coagulant)

## Mechanism of action
- Precipitates and coagulates proteins → chemical cautery; depth of injury depends on concentration (frosting)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- 80–90% TCA: anogenital warts (safe in pregnancy), xanthelasma, small seborrhoeic keratoses
- CROSS technique (65–100%) for ice-pick acne scars
- Chemical peels: 10–20% superficial, 35% medium-depth (often after Jessner's or glycolic) for photoageing, actinic keratoses, pigmentation, scars

## Dose & formulations
- Warts: apply tiny amount with a wooden stick until white frost appears; neutralise excess with talc/bicarbonate; weekly
- Peels: degree of frost guides depth (level I patchy, II white with pink, III solid white); does not need neutralisation

## Adverse effects
- Pain/burning, ulceration if overapplied, scarring
- Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (dark skin), hypopigmentation, infection, herpes reactivation after peels

## Contraindications
- Active infection or herpes at site; keloid tendency, recent isotretinoin (deep peels — relative); unrealistic expectations

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe for warts in pregnancy (not absorbed).

## Viva points
- TCA is safe for warts in pregnancy
- Frosting indicates depth; TCA peels are self-neutralising
- CROSS technique for ice-pick scars

_Sources: Khopkar ch.20, ch.30 and ch.31 (TCA peels); Wolverton 4e ch.53 (Chemical peels). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
